ai.literal: Without investigating, than befriending, ruin there is not; befriended after, release there is not, to those who practice friendship.
ai.translation: There is no greater ruin than making a friend without investigation, for once friendship is made, there is no letting go for those who maintain it.
ai.modern: ஒருவரைப் பற்றி ஆராயாமல் நட்பு கொள்வதை விடப் பெரிய கேடு வேறு இல்லை. ஏனென்றால், நட்பு கொண்ட பிறகு சிறந்த நட்பைக் காப்பவர்களுக்கு அதிலிருந்து விடுதலை இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against rushing into friendships without careful thought. The word 'nāṭātu' means failing to investigate a person's character. 'Naṭṭalin' uses the comparative suffix to show that nothing is worse than such hasty befriending. The reason is given in the second line: for those who truly practice friendship ('naṭpu āḷpavarkku'), there is no 'vīṭu' once the bond is formed. Here, 'vīṭu' means release or abandonment, not its common meaning of a house. Therefore, being stuck with a bad friend brings inevitable ruin.

ai.literal: Having examined, having examined, he who does not take - friendship, in the end, oneself dying sorrow will give.
ai.translation: Forming a friendship without examining the person again and again will ultimately bring sorrow that leads to one's death.
ai.modern: பலமுறை ஆராய்ந்து பார்க்காமல் ஒருவனுடன் கொள்ளும் நட்பு, முடிவில் தான் சாகும் அளவிற்கான துன்பத்தைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against rushing into friendships without thorough and repeated evaluation. The repetition in 'ஆய்ந்து ஆய்ந்து' (examining again and again) emphasizes the need for continuous scrutiny before accepting someone as a friend. If one fails to do this, the resulting friendship will ultimately bring grief severe enough to cause one's own death.

ai.literal: Character and lineage and faults and undiminished kindred and, having known, make friendship.
ai.translation: Make friends only after examining a person's character, lineage, faults, and their unfailing kindred.
ai.modern: ஒருவருடைய குணம், குடும்பப் பின்னணி, குறைகள் மற்றும் குறையாத சுற்றத்தார் ஆகியவற்றை நன்கு ஆராய்ந்து அறிந்த பிறகே அவரிடம் நட்பு கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet lists the essential qualities to investigate before forming a friendship. One must carefully examine a potential friend's good character, family background, personal flaws, and the nature of their constant companions. The word 'அறிந்தியாக்க' emphasizes that friendship should be bound or forged only after thoroughly knowing all these aspects. By weighing both the good and the bad, one ensures a stable and trustworthy relationship.

ai.literal: Good family having been born, in oneself blame him who shrinks from, even having given, acquiring is necessary friendship.
ai.translation: Even by paying a price, one must acquire the friendship of a person born in a good family who shrinks from disgrace.
ai.modern: நல்ல குடியில் பிறந்து தன்னிடம் பழி சேர்வதற்கு வெட்கப்படும் இயல்புடையவனின் நட்பை, ஏதேனும் விலை கொடுத்தாவது பெற்றுக்கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the immense value of befriending someone of noble character. The phrase 'குடி பிறந்து' refers to being born into a respectable family, which instills strong moral values. Such a person will naturally fear and avoid any 'பழி' (blame or disgrace) falling upon themselves ('தன்கண்'). The poet advises that the friendship ('நட்பு') of such a principled individual is so precious that one must acquire it ('கொளல் வேண்டும்') even if it means giving up something valuable in return ('கொடுத்தும்').

ai.literal: To weep having spoken, wrong having rebuked, proper way to know capable persons' friendship having examined take.
ai.translation: Examine and accept the friendship of those capable of moving you to tears with their words, rebuking your wrongdoings, and guiding you to the proper path.
ai.modern: தவறு செய்யும் போது மனம் வருந்தி அழும்படி அறிவுரை கூறியும், தீய வழியில் செல்லும்போது கண்டித்தும், நல்வழியை அறியச் செய்ய வல்லவர்களின் நட்பை ஆராய்ந்து ஏற்றுக்கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the qualities of a true friend whose companionship is worth seeking. A good friend does not merely flatter but has the courage to speak harsh truths that might make one weep for their mistakes. They actively rebuke wrong actions and have the capacity to teach the proper path of conduct. The verse advises that one should carefully examine and secure the friendship of such capable individuals, as their guidance is invaluable.

ai.literal: Even in ruin there is a benefit: relatives (acc.) having stretched that which measures, a rod.
ai.translation: Even in ruin there is a certain benefit: it acts as a measuring rod to stretch out and measure one's true friends.
ai.modern: ஒருவனுக்கு வரும் துன்பத்திலும் ஒரு நன்மை உண்டு; அத்துன்பமே அவனுடைய நண்பர்களின் உண்மையான இயல்பை அளந்து காட்டும் அளவுகோலாக அமையும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet reveals a hidden advantage in facing adversity. The word 'கேடு' refers to ruin or hardship, while 'உறுதி' means a solid benefit or good. The poet uses the metaphor of a measuring rod ('கோல்') that is stretched out ('நீட்டி') to measure things. Hardship acts exactly like this rod, allowing a person to accurately measure the true loyalty and worth of their friends and relatives ('கிளைஞர்'). Thus, adversity is not entirely bad, as it exposes who one's real companions are.

ai.literal: Profit that which is called to a person fools' friendship having abandoned letting go.
ai.translation: The true profit for a person is to abandon and let go of the friendship of fools.
ai.modern: ஒருவருக்கு உண்மையான லாபம் என்று சொல்லப்படுவது, அறிவற்றவர்களின் நட்பை விட்டு விலகிவிடுவதே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines what constitutes a true gain or profit (ஊதியம்) in the context of choosing friends. It states that for any person, the greatest benefit is simply walking away from the friendship of fools (பேதையார் கேண்மை). The word 'ஒரீஇ' (having abandoned) combined with 'விடல்' (letting go) emphasizes a complete and decisive separation. By placing this in the chapter on investigating friendship, the text highlights that avoiding bad company is just as valuable as acquiring good friends.

ai.literal: Do not think of things that diminish the spirit; do not take, in sorrow, the friendship of those who cut off support.
ai.translation: Do not harbor thoughts that diminish your spirit; do not accept the friendship of those who abandon you in times of sorrow.
ai.modern: மன ஊக்கத்தைக் குறைக்கும் செயல்களை எண்ணாதிருக்க வேண்டும்; துன்பம் வந்த காலத்தில் துணையை விட்டு விலகுபவரின் நட்பைக் கொள்ளாதிருக்க வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises against two harmful things: discouraging thoughts and unreliable friends. First, one should not entertain thoughts that shrink the mind or diminish one's spirit. Second, one should never accept the friendship of those who sever their support when sorrow or trouble strikes. The word 'ஆற்று' (the oblique form of 'ஆறு', meaning way or support) combined with 'அறுப்பார்' vividly describes fair-weather friends who cut off their ties and leave one stranded in difficult times.

ai.translation: The friendship of those who abandon you in times of ruin will burn your heart, even if you recall it at the hour of death.
ai.modern: துன்பம் வரும் காலத்தில் நம்மைக் கைவிட்டுச் செல்பவர்களின் நட்பை, நாம் இறக்கும் காலத்தில் நினைத்தாலும் அது நம் மனத்தைச் சுடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against false friends who desert a person when misfortune strikes. The phrase 'keṭum kālai' refers to the time of ruin or adversity, while 'aṭum kālai' refers to the ultimate time of destruction or death. The poet emphasizes the deep emotional scar left by such betrayal. Even at the very end of life, merely recalling the friendship of those who abandoned you will burn your heart with pain.

ai.literal: Let associate blemish-without-those friendship; something even having given, let abandon compatibility-without-those friendship.
ai.translation: Cultivate the friendship of the flawless. Even if you must give something up to do so, abandon the friendship of the incompatible.
ai.modern: குற்றமற்றவர்களின் நட்பை விரும்பி ஏற்றுக்கொள்ள வேண்டும். ஒத்த பண்பு இல்லாதவர்களின் நட்பை, அவர்களுக்கு ஏதாவது ஒரு பொருளைக் கொடுத்தாவது விட்டுவிட வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises on the active choices one must make regarding companions. It urges us to embrace the friendship of those who are flawless in their character. Conversely, it stresses the importance of abandoning friendship with those who lack compatibility or proper conduct, even if it requires giving up something valuable to sever the tie. The phrase 'even having given something' highlights that escaping bad company is worth any material cost.
